nodes.label: Product Editor — standalone print-file generator
nodes.rationale: App is a standalone 300-DPI print-file generator for Printo.in; it never pushes to an internal OMS — delivery is direct download or signed webhook.

nodes.label: Embed session & order-id flow
nodes.rationale: order_id and callback_url never appear in the iframe URL; they flow caller → session DB → proxy cache → X-Order-ID/X-Callback-URL headers → Django.

nodes.label: Server-side auto-orientation (MediaPipe Pose)
nodes.rationale: generateCanvases needs rotation before drawing the preview, so inference runs inline in the gunicorn backend rather than via Celery, avoiding a double-render or delayed preview.

nodes.label: nginx edge proxy service
nodes.rationale: TLS terminates at the origin using a Cloudflare Origin Certificate; depends_on backend service_healthy so a slow backend blocks proxy startup until ready.

nodes.label: Redis durable broker (redis service)
nodes.rationale: noeviction + appendonly so a burst of large cached values can never evict queued render-job messages and in-flight jobs survive a restart; hostname stays 'redis' so REDIS_URL is unchanged.

nodes.label: Redis disposable cache (redis-cache service)
nodes.rationale: allkeys-lru with a hard cap and no volume — evicting a cached layout list is fine and can never touch the broker now that they are separate instances.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL 16 db service
nodes.rationale: Port published on 127.0.0.1 only — Docker port publishing bypasses host firewalls, so 0.0.0.0 would expose Postgres to the internet on prod.

nodes.label: Django + Gunicorn backend service
nodes.rationale: Loopback-only port; 2 GB memory limit so a leak in one Gunicorn worker can't OOM the whole container; self-migrates on boot via entrypoint.

nodes.label: Next.js frontend service
nodes.rationale: AUTH_SECRET uses ${AUTH_SECRET:?...} fail-fast so a missing secret aborts the deploy loudly instead of shipping a forgeable session-signing key.

nodes.label: celery-worker-priority service
nodes.rationale: Listens only to the 'priority' queue so standard-queue backlog never delays time-sensitive renders; healthcheck pings the worker through the broker.

nodes.label: celery-worker-standard service
nodes.rationale: Horizontally scalable (docker compose up --scale celery-worker-standard=N); concurrency auto-detected from CPU count per replica.

nodes.label: celery-beat scheduler service
nodes.rationale: Periodic task scheduler (daily GC at 02:00 UTC); its entrypoint path skips DB migrations — only the web/Gunicorn container migrates.

nodes.label: CI backend tests job
nodes.rationale: Installs a mediapipe-free subset of requirements (grep -vE '^mediapipe') to stay fast, and auto-discovers every services/tests/test_*.py so new suites run without editing the workflow.

nodes.label: CI frontend typecheck / lint / test job
nodes.rationale: pnpm 9.15.9 pinned to match frontend Dockerfile; runs pnpm typecheck, lint, and test --ci on push/PR to main.
nodes.norm_label: ci frontend typecheck / lint / test job

nodes.label: mediapipe==0.10.18 dependency
nodes.rationale: Loaded lazily by services/orientation.py only when the backend handles POST /api/orientation/detect; ~200 MB docker layer cost; Celery workers share the Dockerfile but never import it.

nodes.label: django-csp==3.8 dependency
nodes.rationale: Enables Content-Security-Policy middleware; ships in report-only mode until the policy is validated against Fabric.js unsafe-eval and the embed iframe frame-ancestors.

nodes.label: celery[redis]==5.3.4 dependency
nodes.rationale: Provides the async render queue with priority/standard worker isolation.

nodes.label: Scalar API reference page
nodes.rationale: Renders the OpenAPI schema at /api/schema/ (drf-spectacular) via the Scalar CDN reference component.

nodes.label: Async task rules (self.retry only, on_commit dispatch)
nodes.rationale: Never mix autoretry_for and self.retry() so DB retry_count and Celery's counter stay in sync; MemoryError and SoftTimeLimitExceeded skip retries; dispatch always inside transaction.on_commit().
nodes.norm_label: async task rules (self.retry only, on_commit dispatch)

nodes.label: Path traversal safety guardrail
nodes.rationale: Always validate request-derived file paths (UUID v4 guard on upload_id) to prevent path traversal before opening any derived path.

nodes.label: No AI image-processing guardrail
nodes.rationale: Do not re-introduce background removal or product detection — the app is a print-file generator, not an AI editor.

nodes.label: isExport flag gating guardrail
nodes.rationale: Frame outlines and preview-only overlays are gated by !isExport; both FabricEditor.tsx and fabric-renderer.ts must respect it consistently so they never appear in the download path.

nodes.label: order_id upsert data-integrity guardrail
nodes.rationale: CanvasData is always written via update_or_create(order_id=...) so operator retries and customer resubmissions never crash on a unique-constraint error.

nodes.label: GC skips manual-review orders guardrail
nodes.rationale: Files tied to a requires_manual_review=True order must never be auto-deleted by the garbage collector, even past expiry.

nodes.label: Data retention policy table
nodes.rationale: Supports DPDP compliance (data minimisation + right to erasure) by cataloguing every store of personal data, where it lives, and how it is deleted.

nodes.label: On-demand order purge (DELETE /api/ops/orders/<id>/purge)
nodes.rationale: Ops-only hard-delete of all order-linked rows and files immediately, bypassing the retention timer; shared upload files still referenced by a surviving order are kept; never on the embed-proxy allowlist.

nodes.label: Gap: EmbedSession rows never swept
nodes.rationale: Rows persist past the 2 h token expiry; recommended follow-up is a GC pass deleting sessions older than ~30 days.

nodes.label: Gap: APIRequest rows grow unbounded
nodes.rationale: IP + user-agent are personal data under DPDP; recommended follow-up is a ~90-day retention sweep.

nodes.label: pe-callback webhook contract
nodes.rationale: Signed webhook POSTed to EmbedSession.callback_url on render completion; the task (notify_caller_webhook_task) is source-of-truth if the doc disagrees.

nodes.label: HMAC-SHA256 raw-body signature verification
nodes.rationale: Verify X-Signature against the RAW request bytes with the api_key as secret using constant-time compare; parsing the body before verification breaks the HMAC.

nodes.label: ZIP fetch via download_url + Bearer
nodes.rationale: Stream the 30–500 MB ZIP directly to disk/S3 with the api_key as Bearer auth; downloading inside the webhook handler causes timeouts (10 s limit, up to 6 attempts).

nodes.label: Webhook integration common mistakes
nodes.rationale: Raw-body HMAC, timing-safe compare, out-of-band download, streaming (not in-memory) persistence, and never skipping the HMAC check.

nodes.label: Web-tier load baseline (ApacheBench)
nodes.rationale: /api/health is the unthrottled proxy+gunicorn ceiling; authenticated reads are rate-limited to 200 req/60s per IP so a flood mostly returns 429 (the limiter working, not a throughput number).

nodes.label: Problem: manual preflight bottleneck
nodes.rationale: The bottleneck is the manual design-preflight review between upload and production, taking 1–3 hours/order; target is under 5 minutes fully automated.

nodes.label: Solution Track A — automated preview & validation
nodes.rationale: Customer self-validates via a print-ready preview before checkout; qty mismatch surfaces as empty frames, eliminating the preflight checkpoint.
nodes.norm_label: solution track a — automated preview & validation

nodes.label: B1 — canvas state persistence (IndexedDB + editor_state)
nodes.rationale: Two-layer persistence: server editor_state JSON for transforms/overlays plus client IndexedDB keyed by (orderId, fileId) for original File blobs; refresh restores previews AND the Files needed to re-render.

nodes.label: B2 — async image-generation queue
nodes.rationale: Celery + Redis decouple rendering from the HTTP request cycle so a synchronous render no longer holds a Gunicorn thread and blocks concurrent orders under festival peaks.

nodes.label: B3 — SKU-to-layout mapping
nodes.rationale: JSON-on-disk map with public read (so printo.in resolves SKU before creating a session) and ops-only write; PUT validates every layout_name exists so the file never holds a broken pointer.

nodes.label: B4 — server-side upload + render for large batches
nodes.rationale: Client-side Fabric.js rendering crashed low-RAM devices on 100–200 photos; chunked upload + Celery 300 DPI Pillow render replaced it, and the ≤20-canvas threshold was removed in v1.8 for one unified contract.
nodes.norm_label: b4 — server-side upload + render for large batches

nodes.label: B5 — operations & reliability hardening
nodes.rationale: DEBUG default flipped off, Pillow memory hygiene, GC time limits, multi-stage Dockerfile, healthchecks, django-csp report-only, single-source upload size, ESLint flat config.

nodes.label: B6 — login flow hardening
nodes.rationale: Distinguishes PIA outage (5xx / timeout) from bad credentials (4xx) so users don't retype passwords during an incident; adds 10 s fetch timeout, server-side auth gate, and a per-IP rate limiter.

nodes.label: Standalone generator — no internal OMS push (v1.9)
nodes.rationale: push_to_production_estimator_task was deleted and replaced with notify_caller_webhook_task; the embed webhook gives the storefront everything to attach files, and the storefront talks to OMS via its own existing integration.
nodes.norm_label: standalone generator — no internal oms push (v1.9)

nodes.label: Calendar S3-readiness audit
nodes.rationale: READY — no hardcoded local paths outside settings.STORAGE_ROOT; every calendar path derives from the single env-driven STORAGE_ROOT.

nodes.label: Local-filesystem atomic writes (the one S3 assumption)
nodes.rationale: Three callers do tempfile + os.replace atomic writes; S3 PutObject is already atomic, so each becomes write-temp→upload→delete behind a blob-store shim.
nodes.norm_label: local-filesystem atomic writes (the one s3 assumption)

nodes.label: Proposed services/blob_store.py shim
nodes.rationale: Wrap atomic writes behind a small shim so the three callers stay unchanged when migrating from disk to S3.

nodes.label: Bundled Inter Variable font
nodes.rationale: Single variable font (weights 100–900 in one 859 KB file, SIL OFL 1.1) loaded once per worker via services/fonts.get_font(); falls back to PIL default with a warning if absent.

nodes.label: Do-not-add-more-fonts rule
nodes.rationale: Hardcoding one well-engineered variable font eliminates a class of production failure modes; every other .ttf would be unused dead weight in the image.

nodes.label: Calendar primitive (layout-agnostic region)
nodes.rationale: A positioned {x,y,width,height}-% region owning only the grid/cells/pills/holidays; photo frames and branding stay owned by the layout, so four product types come free from authoring one primitive.

nodes.label: Pre-existing gap: server renders no overlays
nodes.rationale: engine.py had zero ImageDraw/ImageFont — text/shape/image overlays were preview-only and vanished from the print, so server-side overlay rendering is a hard prerequisite for the calendar.
nodes.norm_label: pre-existing gap: server renders no overlays

nodes.label: Phase 1 — server-side overlay rendering (foundation)
nodes.rationale: Builds services/overlay_renderer.py + services/fonts.py and unblocks every existing overlay type, not just the calendar; ships independently as v1.12.

nodes.label: Calendar as a Multi-Surface product (productType flag)
nodes.rationale: Modelling a 12-month calendar as Multi-Surface + a productType tag reuses render/embed/webhook plumbing unchanged; a separate category would fork two render pipelines and two ops UIs.
nodes.norm_label: calendar as a multi-surface product (producttype flag)

nodes.label: Single-template authoring → 12-surface auto-gen
nodes.rationale: Ops designs one representative month; the system materializes 12 surfaces so scaling to 12-month batches doesn't require 12× the design effort or manual sync of global controls.

nodes.label: Per-surface sparse overrides
nodes.rationale: surfaceOverrides is field-level replace (not deep merge) because merging arrays is ambiguous; banned fields (themePreset, calendarType, weekStart, canvas, monthRange) are validator-rejected.

nodes.label: Three calendar theme presets
nodes.rationale: modern-minimalist / modern-genz / weekday-highlight stored as JSON in storage/calendar_styles/; ops picks one and the customer can switch on the preview page (custom-printing concept).

nodes.label: Gen-Z palettes + dotCycle
nodes.rationale: Four coordinated palettes each set all six colour roles plus a 3-slot dotCycle; the customer picks one swatch — picking colour roles individually would invite ugly off-brand combinations.

nodes.label: Global holiday auto-load
nodes.rationale: 5-year seed (2026–2030) for en-IN + generic sourced from Nager.Date at build time, plus an ops upload endpoint for corrections/new locales without a deploy.

nodes.label: CalendarCellOverride (text / image / hide)
nodes.rationale: Overrides key by globally-unique ISO date (not tile position) so photo-canvas count and English↔Financial flips can never lose or misplace an entry.

nodes.label: Pill-style cell entries (cap 3, dot cycle)
nodes.rationale: Pill background is a single theme colour; dot colour rotates through a 3-slot per-theme cycle by entry index so multi-entry cells stay distinguishable without giving the customer a picker.

nodes.label: Auto-rolling year (defaultYear: current)
nodes.rationale: Resolves at editor mount via Date() so layout files never freeze to a specific year — a 2026 layout auto-prints 2027 from Jan 1 with zero ops intervention.

nodes.label: Calendar type (English vs Financial)
nodes.rationale: Customer toggle on the same SKU drives startMonth (1 vs 4) and baseYear derivation; the 12 surfaces re-derive instantly, so English and Financial are one SKU.

nodes.label: Design principle — minimal customer-facing controls
nodes.rationale: Templates-not-configurators: every knob is a chance to produce off-brand output, so controls are the smallest set that serves the use case; want more → pick a different layout.

nodes.label: Shared month-grid math (client + server identical)
nodes.rationale: Both renderers compute the 28/35/42-cell grid the same way so the editor preview matches the 300 DPI print; parity is pinned by shared fixtures in CI.

nodes.label: Surface → (year, month) resolution formula
nodes.rationale: totalOffset = surfaceIndex + (calendarMonthOffset ?? 0) handles both multi-surface (12×1) and multi-calendar single-page (1×12) modes uniformly under the constraint count × calendars.length === 12.

nodes.label: MAX_ENTRIES=3 user-first precedence
nodes.rationale: Reverses the original holidays-first rule — user entries fill slots first, holidays fill the rest, overflow is silently suppressed (no +N badge); removing a user entry re-surfaces a suppressed holiday.

nodes.label: Single bundled default font, no picker (§11.7)
nodes.rationale: Renderer uses Inter Variable for every text element; no picker means no font drift between preview and 300 DPI render and eliminates the font-missing production failure mode.
nodes.norm_label: single bundled default font, no picker (§11.7)

nodes.label: v2 S3 download path readiness (§11.17)
nodes.rationale: v1 keeps download_url, RenderJobDownloadView, and engine output paths S3-friendly so the v2 swap (browser fetches signed S3 URL, skipping the Next.js proxy) is a contained change, not a refactor.

nodes.label: Photobook — future productType
nodes.rationale: Multi-Surface is the generic substrate for designed-once-replicated-N products; photobook reuses render/embed/ZIP/webhook and adds only its own ops+preview UIs. productType is the extension point.

nodes.label: Calendar primitive HTML mockup
nodes.rationale: Self-contained interactive mockup visualising only the calendar primitive — grid, cells, pills, holiday auto-load, three theme presets, English/Financial toggle, and per-cell editing.
